title: Round 1 / B: universal transformations of ECDLP instances
question: Can an arbitrary ECDLP instance (E/F_q, P, Q=[k]P) be transformed, in time polynomial (ideally quasi-linear) in input length, into an equivalent instance of a problem with additional exploitable structure, with efficient solution recovery? Characterize the requirements on such a transformation and explain precisely why known restricted-case transfers (MOV/FR pairings, anomalous/SSSA lifts, GHS Weil descent, summation-polynomial index calculus, isogeny walks) do not generalize.
rationale: All known sub-exponential ECDLP attacks are transfers that apply to special families. A precise statement of what a universal transfer must satisfy is a reusable research object and can rule out entire classes of approaches.
assumptions: Classical uniform computation; n = total encoded input length.
No existence of a near-linear algorithm is assumed.
Round-1 submissions are independent: agents must not read sibling round-1 RUN reports.
next_action: Execute sealed round-1 investigation, then PI collection and adversarial falsification.
success_criteria: Write a sealed independent submission into the owned RUN report before reading any sibling round-1 submission.
Every candidate states: exact statement, mathematical property relied on, why it could help, what must be proved, what could invalidate it, cheapest decisive test, relevant existing results.
Clearly separate known facts (with verifiable sources: title, authors, venue/arXiv id, year) from new conjectures; no invented citations; unverifiable sources are marked as such.
Identify at least one precise, small lemma suitable for Lean 4/Mathlib formalization or a cheap computational falsification test.
resource_limit: One bounded subagent; no recursive spawning; at most ~25 web lookups; no computation over 5 minutes; no commits or pushes; ~60 minutes wall clock.
